run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T09:47:43Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because cart-dependent requests through the proxy exceed the proxy's ~15 s upstream timeout and are answered with HTTP 504. The originating failure is the cart service's Redis backend: from 09:45:45Z the cart container logs 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' and every cart error span (84 in the 76-minute window) carries the exact text "Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() ... line 97", while cart's own Redis command spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) fall to zero by ~09:53:47Z. Cart then holds requests for 358-501 s and returns gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION, which frontend turns into HTTP 500 on /api/cart and /api/checkout and checkout turns into PlaceOrder failures with the same 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' text; frontend-proxy's ingress spans for those same traces are 504 at ~15.0 s, which is what the alert measures (961 error spans on span_name 'ingress', 0 on 'router frontend egress'; ingress error rate went from 0 at 09:28:47Z to 0.567/s at 09:48:47Z and 1.463/s at 09:53:47Z). The cart container's VALKEY_ADDR (valkey-cart:6379) matches the valkey-cart Service (port 6379) and its endpoint (100.96.2.228), and the valkey-cart pod is Running with restartCount 0, so the workload is reachable at the IP level but its Redis process is not answering clients; supporting this, the otel-collector redisreceiver's redis_* series (used memory, CPU time counters) stop changing at 09:47:43Z and are frozen through the end of data. Why the valkey-cart container stopped serving could not be read (its logs returned no data and there is no exec tool); the Deployment sets no readiness/liveness probe and very small limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi), and the redisreceiver-reported RSS (9.74 MB) conflicts with the pod's cgroup RSS (3.4 MB), so memory exhaustion is only a hypothesis. frontend-proxy itself is not the origin (its egress spans show the upstream failure and its pod is Running with 0 restarts), and node-level failure is not supported (other workloads on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae kept serving, node conditions normal). Small flagd EventStream error counts on ad/fraud-detection/recommendation and the FailedKillPod/Killing events for an already-deleted cart pod are unrelated to this cause.

claims.text: Over 2026-11-16T08:47:43Z-10:03:47Z frontend-proxy recorded 961.29 error spans, all on span_name 'ingress' (16215.8 unset-status ingress spans), and 0 error spans on span_name 'router frontend egress'.

frontend-proxy's ingress error rate was 0 at 09:28:47Z, 0.0111/s at 09:33:47Z, 0.0037/s at 09:38:47Z, 0.0111/s at 09:43:47Z, then rose to 0.5667/s at 09:48:47Z, 1.4630/s at 09:53:47Z and 0.7167/s at 09:58:47Z, matching the alert start of 09:47:43Z.

The sampled frontend-proxy error spans are operation 'ingress' with tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of about 15.0 s (e.g. 15,001,202 us, 15,000,077 us), each paired with a 'router frontend egress' span of the same ~15.0 s and http.status_code="0", so the 504 is the proxy's own upstream timeout.

cart recorded 84 error spans in the window, on POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (45.23) and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (38.77), with the exact error text "Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() in /usr/src/app/src/cartstore/ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 97" and span durations of 358-501 s.

The cart pod's log shows 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 2026-11-16T09:45:45.9403003Z, followed by repeated 'Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised.' lines from 09:48:03.3406934Z through 09:54:19.2420534Z.

cart's Redis command spans stopped: HGET 3.87/s at 09:43:47Z, 2.78/s at 09:48:47Z and 0 from 09:53:47Z on (HMSET/EXPIRE identical pattern), while cart's server span rates collapsed from 0.94/s (AddItem) and 1.80/s (GetCart) at 09:48:47Z to 0.07/s and 0.04/s at 09:53:47Z and 10:03:47Z.

frontend recorded 256.39 error spans in the window, including POST /api/cart 46.31, GET /api/cart 31.53, 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 79.34, POST /api/checkout 7.12, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 7.12, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 46.31 and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 31.53; the sampled frontend spans carry http.status_code 500 and grpc status 9 FAILED_PRECONDITION with the same 'Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis' text.

checkout is also failing on the same dependency: 6.75 error spans on oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (rpc.grpc.status_code 9) and 6.75 on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) with the detail "cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: rpc error: code = FailedPrecondition desc = Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis".

The cart Deployment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart), the valkey-cart Service exposes port 6379 to selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and the valkey-cart endpoint resolves to pod IP 100.96.2.228 (targetRef valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr), so the address configuration and Service/Endpoint wiring are consistent.

The valkey-cart pod is Running with condition Ready=True, restartCount 0 and container startedAt 2026-11-16T09:14:40Z; its Deployment (image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi) defines no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe, so Ready=True is not backed by any health check of the Redis process.

The otel-collector's redisreceiver series stopped changing at 09:47:43Z: redis_memory_used_bytes is frozen at 1,710,360 bytes from 09:47:43Z onward (last change 09:46:43Z), and redis_cpu_time_seconds_total in all five states (user/sys/user_main_thread/sys_main_thread/user_children/sys_children) is frozen from 09:47:43Z through the last sample at 09:54:43Z.

The cart container stayed up (no restart marks) but its CPU behaviour changed: usage rate rose from ~0.009 cores (09:29-09:46Z) to 0.027 cores at 09:55Z, CFS throttled-period ratio rose from 0.17-0.24 to 0.74-0.90 between 09:50Z and 10:00Z, and working set grew from ~56 MB to ~97 MB against a 165Mi memory limit.

No pod in otel-demo restarted and all 21 pods are Running with restartCount 0 (including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-6rwg6, cart-755465879b-t9mf7 and valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr); nodes i-00702f4ac4662cf00, i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, i-0a709b85c49d987be and i-0ce6a871fe1b79be report Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False.

Only two Kubernetes events fell inside the window for otel-demo, both about the already-deleted pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s: FailedKillPod at 09:50:32Z and Killing at 09:50:33Z; no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy or restart event was returned for valkey-cart or cart.

Error spans by service over the window: frontend-proxy 961.29, frontend 256.39, cart 84, checkout 13.5, recommendation 3.05, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04, accounting 0 and payment 0; the ad/fraud-detection/recommendation errors are on flagd EventStream spans (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) and are not cart-related, while no error series were returned for currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping or image-provider even though those services kept recording spans (e.g. product-catalog 17470, currency 2040, quote 2136, email 2869, shipping 2133, image-provider 183).

Primary cause: the cart service's Redis backend stopped serving clients. cart's own error text names ValkeyCartStore/redis, its Redis command spans cease, the collector's redisreceiver counters freeze at 09:47:43Z, and the valkey-cart pod's Ready=True is meaningless because no readiness probe is configured - so the pod can be reported ready while its Redis process answers nobody. Consequence chain: cart hangs then fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION -> frontend/checkout return 500 after 358-501 s -> frontend-proxy's ~15 s upstream timeout returns 504 -> ingress error rate > 0 -> alert.

Alternative candidate not established: the valkey-cart container's very small resource limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) may have put the Redis process under memory/CPU pressure. Against it: the pod's cgroup RSS is only 3.0-3.45 MB with max usage 5.69 MB against the 10Mi limit, restartCount is 0 with no OOMKilled mark, and its CFS throttled-period ratio is only 0.02-0.07; the redisreceiver-reported redis_memory_rss_bytes of 9.74 MB conflicts with the cgroup figures, so this candidate cannot be confirmed from these metrics.

Alternative candidate not established: cart's 45m CPU quota (CFS throttled-period ratio up to ~0.90) may have stretched cart request handling to the observed 358-501 s. The throttling rise (0.44 at 09:48:43Z, 0.74 at 09:50:43Z) follows the 09:45:45Z 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' log line and the request pile-up, so the evidence does not show it as the trigger; it is more consistent with a consequence.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself as the origin of the errors. Its pod is Running with restartCount 0, all its error spans are ingress responses that mirror a ~15.0 s 'router frontend egress' span and an upstream frontend span of the same duration, and the same ingress operation also returned http.status_code 200 for other requests in the same window - the proxy is reporting an upstream timeout, not failing on its own.

Rejected: a node-level failure on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (where both cart and valkey-cart run). Other workloads on that node kept serving without error evidence (frontend-proxy, product-catalog, checkout, quote, email, accounting, load-generator, postgresql, fraud-detection all have pods there), the node reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False, and the error series are confined to cart-dependent operations rather than to that node's workloads.

Rejected: a cart-side address/Service misconfiguration. The cart Deployment's VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 matches the valkey-cart Service port 6379 and the endpoint 100.96.2.228, and the pod's init container wait-for-valkey-cart completed successfully at 09:14:41Z, so the name/port wiring resolved and worked before the failure.

Have a human inspect and, if needed, restart the valkey-cart pod/container and verify Redis reachability from inside the cart pod (e.g. a PING against valkey-cart:6379); the pod being Ready is not evidence of Redis health because no readiness/liveness probe is defined.

Add a readiness/liveness probe to the valkey-cart container and review its limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) plus cart's Redis connect/semaphore behavior, which currently lets requests be held 358-501 s, and review frontend-proxy's ~15 s upstream timeout against those long dependency stalls.

gaps: The valkey-cart container's logs returned no data for the authorized window and there is no exec/shell tool in this Run, so the in-container reason the Redis process stopped answering (and whether it can still serve PING) is unknown; no OOMKilled/Evicted mark or container restart exists to explain it.
The valkey-cart pod has no readiness/liveness probe and no previous container instance, so its own service health at 09:45-09:47Z cannot be verified from pod status alone.

The otel-collector container's logs also returned no data, so the redisreceiver's own connection errors to the Redis target could not be read; the redisreceiver-reported redis_memory_rss_bytes (9.74 MB) disagrees with the pod cgroup RSS (3.0-3.45 MB), so which process/instance those redis_* series describe is not fully verified.
The NetworkPolicy query returned an empty/no_data view, so whether any NetworkPolicy could have affected cart-to-valkey traffic is unknown.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so whether the valkey-cart resources/probes/image or the cart image/config changed before 09:45Z cannot be determined.

Metric and trace evidence is a sampled/partial view: trace span counts are not unique request counts and the traces shown are a biased sample, so the exact number of user requests that failed cannot be stated.
Object state from Kubernetes is the state at query time, not at 09:45Z, so earlier pod/deployment state is unknown.
next_steps: Human: inspect the valkey-cart pod/container directly (process state, Redis INFO/PING, dmesg/cgroup OOM counters on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) to determine why the Redis process stopped answering at ~09:45Z.
Human: compare the valkey-cart and cart manifests against the intended baseline (limits, probes) and check deployment history via the change-history integration, which is not available here.
Human: after valkey-cart is serving again, confirm cart's HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE span rate recovers and that frontend-proxy ingress error rate returns to 0.
